definitions.explanation: A natural number greater than 1 that has no positive divisors other than 1 and itself.

examples.japanese: {素数|そすう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{無限|むげん}→無限：00296_mugen⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{存在|そんざい}する→存在する：17185_sonzaisuru⟧。
examples.english: There are infinitely many prime numbers.

examples.japanese: 100⟦{以下|いか}→以下：01294_ika⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{素数|そすう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧すべて⟦{書|か}き{出|だ}し→書き出す：13053_kakidasu⟧⟦なさい→なさる：01307_nasaru⟧。
examples.english: Write out all the prime numbers up to 100.

notes:
Composed of {素|そ} (basic/elemental) + ⟦{数|すう}→数：03360_suu⟧ (number), suggesting a number in its most basic, indivisible form. A fundamental term in mathematics.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {素数|そすう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{求|もと}める→求める：02316_motomeru⟧: to find a prime number
- {素数|そすう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{判定|はんてい}→判定：09767_hantei⟧: primality test
- ⟦{最大|さいだい}→最大：04827_saidai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{素数|そすう}: the largest prime number
- {素数|そすう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{一覧|いちらん}→一覧：17694_ichiran⟧: a list of prime numbers

RELATED WORDS:
- {合成数|ごうせいすう}: composite number — a number that is not prime (has divisors other than 1 and itself)
- {因数|いんすう}: factor — a number that divides another evenly
- {素因数分解|そいんすうぶんかい}: prime factorization — breaking a number into its prime factors

CULTURAL NOTE:
Prime numbers appear in Japanese pop culture, notably in the manga and anime series featuring mathematical themes. The concept is taught in Japanese middle school mathematics.
